newsitem.title: USA: Cold leaves Sun with no heating oil in NYH. [CORRECTED 22:08 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Cold leaves Sun with no heating oil in NYH. [CORRECTED 22:08 GMT]

text.p: An early spring cold spell in the Northeast has left Sun Co Inc, a major supplier of heating oil in the region, without any heating oil for distributors until late next week, a Sun spokesman said.
"We don't have any product available now," said Bud Davis. "This is not uncommon at the shoulder of the the season."
While not leaving Sun scrambling for barrels to cover contractual obligations, Davis said other parties will no doubt take out those hungry buyers at lofty prices.
"We're not allocating. But there's a market out there. If we don't have any, someone else sure does," Davis said.

"At the end of a heating oil season, we are not normally in full heating oil production. And when you have a cold spell, bulk contract customers (corrects from "distributors") come to their suppliers," Davis said.
A week ago, cash differentials on heating oil jumped nearly a cent, with deals since then heard closed around the 4.00 cents over May NYMEX level.
But the strength is focused on the front end of the market, underscoring that the tightness in the heating oil markets is transitional and should ease once spring sheds its autumn-like chill.
((-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk, 1 212 859 1633))
